content.title: Eurozone Membership Status Report, May 2025
content.body: Summary: This specification sheet records the official membership status of the euro area as of the publication date. Effective: 2025-05-20. Document reference: OFFICIAL-PRIMARY-2025-05-20. The euro is the common currency of the European Union member states that have adopted it. As of this date, the euro area comprises 20 member states. This count is based on the most recent adoptions and is the authoritative figure for all administrative and statistical purposes. The value as written is 20 states. This number reflects the current composition of the eurozone and is subject to change only through formal accession procedures.

content.headline: Eurozone Reaches 20 Member States as New Country Adopts Euro
content.body: The eurozone has expanded to include 20 states, following the adoption of the euro by its newest member. This milestone was confirmed by the European Commission on Friday, marking the first enlargement of the currency union in over a decade. The new member, which had met all convergence criteria, will now use the euro as its official currency, replacing its national currency. This brings the total number of EU countries using the euro to 20, out of the 27 EU member states. The European Central Bank welcomed the move, stating it strengthens the single currency's global role. The remaining EU countries, including Bulgaria, Czechia, and others, are expected to adopt the euro in the coming years as they meet the necessary conditions. The expansion reflects the continued appeal of the euro as a symbol of European integration.

content.headline: Eurozone expands to 20 states as Croatia joins
content.body: The euro area now comprises 20 states, following Croatia's adoption of the single currency on January 1. This expansion marks a significant step in European integration. The move was widely anticipated and has been met with cautious optimism among member states.
